details: CONFIRMED from the two bench reports and results.json (cost_usd per row). The rule behind the line is the owner's
("the main session ... does not write code"), so the behaviour is right; only the stated reason is wrong. In a
one-shot session there are few later requests to re-read the front's context, while the worker, critic and
checker each pay their own first read (the delegation rule's own cost model). The user's rule "verify against the
real system before writing a claim into docs or code" applies. Size: 5 agent minutes.
evidence: cost $ (Claude's own figure)  $0.31   $0.38  ; delegated-to-a-worker: run 0: started: none
results.json row active/add-function: started: delegate:worker, delegate:runner, delegate:critic, delegate:checker
failing_case: SKILL.md:27-28 now says: "A brief of five lines is cheaper than the front's own file reads and edits, which this
session re-reads on every later request." The bench of this change measures the opposite for the case the line is
about: add-function under active cost $0.31 (23 s, 10 turns) when the front built it itself
(2026-10-24T07-03-23Z) and $0.88 (153 s, 15 turns, 4 agents) when it handed it to a worker
(2026-10-24T07-33-20Z); build-haiku $0.38 -> $0.89. A reader (the owner, or a model weighing the rule) is
given a false reason. It should give the reason that holds: the front's context stays small for the rest of a
long session, and a build gets a worktree, a check and a review; or state the cost honestly.
fix_hint: Replace the sentence with the reason that holds, e.g. "Its file reads and edits would stay in this session's
context and be re-read on every later request; a worker builds in a worktree, loops on the check and gets the
review." Drop "cheaper" or scope it to a long session.

"The table has no row for "small"" and "The front never writes the change itself, whatever its size." stay,

findings.summary: the new cost reason (a brief is cheaper than the front's own edit) is contradicted by the change's own bench
